note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 4-weeks postpartum woman with sudden-onset shortness of breath at rest, new dry cough, and perceived tachycardia; high concern for pulmonary embolism; advised urgent hospital evaluation and to avoid codeine.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath (SOB) beginning ~1 hour prior to call while sitting and watching TV.
- Timeline:
  - Yesterday: New cough, non-productive.
  - Today (within last hour): SOB at rest; feels heart “really going.”
  - 4 weeks ago: Cesarean section.
- Symptom details:
  - SOB onset sudden; patient unsure if worsening over call.
  - Chest: No frank chest pain at rest; reports chest soreness with deep inspiration.
  - Palpitations: Feels heart racing; patient appears stressed.
  - Cough: Dry; no sputum reported.
- Associated symptoms/pertinent negatives:
  - Denies chest pain at rest.
  - No syncope or hemoptysis mentioned.
  - No leg symptoms (swelling/pain) elicited.
  - Baby reported well; no sick contacts at home.
- Prior similar episodes: None.
- Recent illness: Last cough/cold “a good few months ago.”

Past Medical History:
- Postpartum status s/p cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Otherwise denies other medical problems.

Medications/Allergies:
- Codeine for post-op pain; taken regularly after C-section but none for ~1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented). Advised not to take currently.
- Allergy: Ibuprofen; reaction not specified.

Social History:
- Postpartum at home with baby; currently alone; partner at work.
- Plans to self-transport to hospital with baby per clinician advice.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not documented.
- Travel/immobility beyond postpartum recovery: Not documented.

Family History:
- Mother with history of leg clots (DVT).

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth encounter; no formal exam.
- Vitals:
  - Patient pulse count: 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as slightly tachycardic.
  - No SpO2, blood pressure, respiratory rate, or temperature recorded.
- No additional exam findings documented.

Investigations:
- None performed during the call.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath in a 4-weeks postpartum patient (s/p C-section) with pleuritic-type chest soreness and perceived tachycardia.
  - Assessment: High concern for pulmonary embolism (PE) given postpartum status and acute onset at rest; DVT/PE risk supported by family history (maternal DVT). Alternative considerations include viral URI/acute bronchitis, anxiety-related dyspnea, pneumonia, or less likely peripartum cardiomyopathy per DDx.
  - Plan:
    - Immediate hospital evaluation recommended to rule out PE/DVT (patient elected to self-transport promptly).
    - Advised to avoid taking codeine for now.
    - Bring necessary items for baby; proceed “fairly quickly.”
    - Ambulance was offered; patient declined.
    - Hospital to evaluate and treat if clot identified (e.g., anticoagulation per hospital protocol).
- Issue 2: New dry cough since yesterday.
  - Assessment: Could represent viral URI/acute bronchitis; however, abrupt SOB and postpartum VTE risk keep PE highest on differential.
  - Plan: Will be assessed as part of urgent hospital evaluation.
- Issue 3: Palpitations/tachycardia and anxiety/stress.
  - Assessment: May be reactive to dyspnea/pain/anxiety; tachycardia could also reflect PE.
  - Plan: Monitor and evaluate in hospital setting.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Pulmonary embolism (High):
  - Sudden SOB at rest, pleuritic soreness with deep breath, postpartum 4 weeks after C-section, perceived tachycardia; family history of DVT.
- Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis (Medium):
  - New dry cough; less consistent with sudden rest-onset SOB and pleuritic features.
- Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea (Low–Medium):
  - Reports stress and heart racing; does not fully explain pleuritic soreness or postpartum VTE risk.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Full vital signs (SpO2, BP, RR, temperature), full ROS (fever, chills, hemoptysis, leg swelling/pain, orthopnea/PND, edema), detailed obstetric history (preeclampsia/HTN, postpartum course, breastfeeding), VTE risk factors (smoking, recent travel/immobility beyond postoperative period, hormonal therapy), comprehensive medication list and dosages, allergy reaction details.
  - Objective duration of pulse count interval not documented; true HR cannot be calculated from “30 beats” alone.
- Conflicts:
  - DOB stated as 1980 initially; later “1983” mentioned by clinician—conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor pauses; no major inaudible sections.
